topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives for cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Traditional cancer treatment modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore conventional methods of cancer treatment, focusing on surgical resection, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy alongside their mechanisms and systemic toxicities.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic biological weaknesses in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failures, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene-targeted therapies and kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how hyperactivated oncogenes, particularly protein kinases, are targeted with small-molecule inhibitors, along with the subsequent emergence of drug resistance and bypass pathways.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the design and therapeutic mechanisms of engineered antibodies that target cell-surface antigens either directly or by delivering cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell redirection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the role of the immune system in cancer control and the therapeutic activation or engineering of T cells using checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Overall challenges, progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on the historical progress, biological complexities, clinical dilemmas, and evolving strategies that shape the future of cancer treatment.
